svg.title: The Wrap Machine, From Target List to Servicer
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-wrap-mechanics-process-flow; chapter number: 1; title: The Wrap Machine, From Target List to Servicer; subtitle: Mirror wrap in, equity wrap out, spread earned on the full balance; caption: Five steps practitioners describe for laying a larger wrap note over a live underlying loan, with the buyer paying the wrap holder and a servicer paying the original lender first.; assumptions note: Targeting filters come from Chris Goff's nationwide query; buy-side and sell-side structures come from Bill Brunchick; servicing order comes from Scott Horne. No figures beyond those reported are implied.; note: Sources: Chris Goff (X_UODDIMvFs), Bill Brunchick with Kris Haskins (kM__5b36grI), Scott Horne's Owner Finance Network (VDXOvtqzbZk).; chart type: process_flow; stages: step: 01; label: Pull Absentee-Owner Targets; value: Step 1; detail: Chris Goff filters absentee owners with values above $300,000, at least 20% equity and two-plus years of ownership; his nationwide query returned 7,284,401 properties.; step: 02; label: Buy on a Mirror Wrap; value: Step 2; detail: Brunchick buys on a mirror wrap when there is little or no equity, matching the underlying terms.; step: 03; label: Sell on an Equity Wrap; value: Step 3; detail: Mark up both price and rate so the spread runs on the full balance; Brunchick shows 6% on $20,000 of equity plus a 2% gap on an $80,000 first at 4%.; step: 04; label: Record the Security Instrument; value: Step 4; detail: Never record the note itself; record the deed of trust or mortgage with the wraparound rider (Brunchick).; step: 05; label: Board a Payment Servicer; value: Step 5; detail: Scott Horne routes every payment through a servicer that pays the underlying lender first and the seller last, the industry's fraud preventer.

text.title: The Wrap Machine, From Target List to Servicer
text.tspan: The Wrap Machine, From Target List to Servicer

rect.title: step: 01; label: Pull Absentee-Owner Targets; value: Step 1; detail: Chris Goff filters absentee owners with values above $300,000, at least 20% equity and two-plus years of ownership; his nationwide query returned 7,284,401 properties.

text.title: Chris Goff filters absentee owners with values above $300,000, at least 20% equity and two-plus years of ownership; his nationwide query returned 7,284,401 properties.

rect.title: step: 02; label: Buy on a Mirror Wrap; value: Step 2; detail: Brunchick buys on a mirror wrap when there is little or no equity, matching the underlying terms.

text.title: Brunchick buys on a mirror wrap when there is little or no equity, matching the underlying terms.

rect.title: step: 03; label: Sell on an Equity Wrap; value: Step 3; detail: Mark up both price and rate so the spread runs on the full balance; Brunchick shows 6% on $20,000 of equity plus a 2% gap on an $80,000 first at 4%.

text.title: Mark up both price and rate so the spread runs on the full balance; Brunchick shows 6% on $20,000 of equity plus a 2% gap on an $80,000 first at 4%.

rect.title: step: 04; label: Record the Security Instrument; value: Step 4; detail: Never record the note itself; record the deed of trust or mortgage with the wraparound rider (Brunchick).

text.title: Never record the note itself; record the deed of trust or mortgage with the wraparound rider (Brunchick).

rect.title: step: 05; label: Board a Payment Servicer; value: Step 5; detail: Scott Horne routes every payment through a servicer that pays the underlying lender first and the seller last, the industry's fraud preventer.

text.title: Scott Horne routes every payment through a servicer that pays the underlying lender first and the seller last, the industry's fraud preventer.

Assumptions: Targeting filters come from Chris Goff's nationwide query; buy-side and sell-side structures come from Bill Brunchick; servicing order comes from Scott Horne. No figures beyond those reported are implied.
